title: Call centres: Are you talking to AI?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: calm down someone who is angry
very soon, within a short time
used to add emphasis to a statement, to give more detail about what has just been said, or to introduce something that contrasts with it
able to put yourself into someone else’s position and share their feelings or experiences
(filler word) used to give the speaker time to think, or to express uncertainty

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《六分钟英语》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Pippa. Have you ever phoned up a company and had your call held in a queue?
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Pippa。你有没有给哪家公司打过电话，然后被放在队列里等待？

sentences.en: If you have, then you've probably heard messages like this: Hello.
sentences.zh: 如果你有过，那你大概听过这样的提示：你好。

sentences.en: Your call is important to us. You are number 89 in the queue.
sentences.zh: 你的来电对我们很重要。你在队列中排第89位。

sentences.en: If you'd like to continue to hold, press 1.
sentences.zh: 如果你想继续等待，请按1。

sentences.en: If you'd like to return to the main menu, press 0.
sentences.zh: 如果你想返回主菜单，请按0。

sentences.en: How do you feel when your phone call is put on hold, Phil?
sentences.zh: Phil，当你的电话被挂起等待时，你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Oh, frustrated usually, although I do like it when there's a number saying how many people are in front of you.
sentences.zh: 哦，通常会感到沮丧，虽然如果有数字告诉你前面有多少人在排队，我确实会觉得好点。

sentences.en: That's good. Well, when your call is finally connected, it's usually a call centre worker you'll speak to – a real live person who'll hopefully fix your problem.
sentences.zh: 那倒是不错。嗯，当你的电话终于接通时，通常和你对话的是呼叫中心的工作人员——一个真正的活人，他希望能帮你解决问题。

sentences.en: But increasingly, this work is now done using artificial intelligence, or AI.
sentences.zh: 但现在，这项工作越来越多地开始使用人工智能，也就是AI来完成。

sentences.en: And this is causing problems in countries like India and the Philippines, where call centre jobs make up a big part of the economy.
sentences.zh: 这正在印度和菲律宾等国家引发问题，在这些国家，呼叫中心的工作占据了经济很大的一部分。

sentences.en: In this programme, we'll be asking who's really in charge at the call centre: humans or AI?
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们要问的是：呼叫中心到底谁说了算：人类还是AI？

sentences.en: As always, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们会学习一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And remember you can read along with the programme, and find the list of new words and phrases, by visiting our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以通过访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，一边阅读节目内容，一边查找新单词和短语列表。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 但现在我有一个问题要问你，Phil。

sentences.en: Around the world, numbers of call centre workers have grown rapidly in recent years.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，近年来呼叫中心员工的数量增长迅速。

sentences.en: If you're listening to this, maybe you're a call centre worker yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在听这个节目，也许你自己就是一名呼叫中心员工。

sentences.en: So, approximately how many people work in call centres globally, Phil?
sentences.zh: 那么，Phil，全球大约有多少人在呼叫中心工作？

sentences.en: Is it: a) 7 million? b) 17 million? or, c) 27 million?
I think b) 17 million. OK, well you'll have to listen to the end to find out the answer.
sentences.zh: 我猜是 b) 1700万。好吧，你得听到最后才能知道答案。

sentences.en: Now, one worker worried about the impact of AI on jobs in the Philippines is Mylene Cabalona, president of the call centre workers' union, B.I.E.N.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一位员工对AI对菲律宾就业的影响感到担忧，她叫Mylene Cabalona，是呼叫中心工会B.I.E.N.的主席。

sentences.en: Here, she tells BBC World Service programme, 'Tech Life', about some of the difficulties of her job, and why she fears for the future: So, and this person is quite already aggravated, and he keeps on yelling and that's the, you know, that's the difficult part because the mental stress also… you know, you have to pacify the client, and you have to make sure you're able to resolve the concern.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向BBC世界服务部的节目“Tech Life”讲述了她工作中的一些困难，以及她为什么对未来感到恐惧：所以，这个人已经相当恼火了，他一直在大喊大叫，你知道的，这就是困难的部分，因为心理压力也……你知道的，你必须安抚客户，你必须确保你能解决他们的问题。

sentences.en: And then the difficult part on that conversation is that you're being monitored by an AI.
sentences.zh: 然后在对话中困难的部分是，你正在受到AI的监视。

sentences.en: I mean, eventually AI would replace… us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最终AI会取代……我们。

sentences.en: It's going to displace workers… you know, eventually, in the near future.
sentences.zh: 它将取代工人……你知道的，最终，在不久的将来。

sentences.en: Even, as a matter of fact, there's been a study that says that about 300,000 workers or around 27% of workers that's going to be displaced because of AI, and that's slowly happening.
sentences.zh: 甚至，事实上，曾有一项研究表明，大约30万名工人，即大约27%的工人将被AI取代，而这正在慢慢发生。

sentences.en: Call centre work involves dealing with customers who've phoned up to complain.
sentences.zh: 呼叫中心的工作包括应对打电话来投诉的客户。

sentences.en: They're often angry, aggravated and yelling, or shouting, down the phone.
sentences.zh: 他们经常很生气、很恼火，在电话里大吼大叫。

sentences.en: It's Mylene's job to pacify them, to calm them down.
sentences.zh: Mylene的工作就是安抚他们，让他们平静下来。

sentences.en: If that wasn't stressful enough, Mylene's conversations are monitored by AI systems to see how well she fixes her clients' problems.
sentences.zh: 如果这还不够有压力的话，Mylene的对话还会受到AI系统的监控，以看她解决客户问题的能力如何。

sentences.en: You might think AI was built to support workers like Mylene, but she fears AI will replace her in the near future, a phrase meaning 'very soon' or 'within a short time'.
sentences.zh: 你可能认为AI是用来支持像Mylene这样的工人的，但她担心AI在不久的将来会取代她，“不久的将来”是一个意思是“非常快”或“在很短时间内”的短语。

sentences.en: Mylene emphasises her fears about being replaced by giving details about a study she read, which claimed that 27% of workers will be displaced by AI.
sentences.zh: Mylene通过提供她读过的一项研究的细节来强调她对被取代的恐惧，该研究称27%的工人将被AI取代。

sentences.en: She uses the phrase, as a matter of fact, to emphasise what she's saying, and to give more detail as evidence to support it.
sentences.zh: 她使用了“事实上”这个短语来强调她所说的话，并提供更多细节作为支持它的证据。

sentences.en: But Mylene thinks AI will never fully replace humans.
sentences.zh: 但Mylene认为AI永远不会完全取代人类。

sentences.en: She says AI lacks one important quality, empathy.
sentences.zh: 她说AI缺少一个重要的品质，那就是同理心。

sentences.en: Here, she explains more to BBC World Service's, 'Tech Life': Well, I don't think AI is, you know, empathetic, or… whenever they talk, I mean if ever a machine or a robot talks to them, you know, people are more compassionate than, you know, when you talk to a robot.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向BBC世界服务部的“Tech Life”节目解释了更多：嗯，我不认为AI是，你知道的，有同理心的，或者……每当它们说话时，我的意思是，如果机器或机器人跟他们说话，你知道的，人们比你跟机器人说话时更有同情心。

sentences.en: Mylene says that AI is not empathetic. Unlike humans, it can't put itself in someone else's place and share their feelings or experiences.
sentences.zh: Mylene说AI没有同理心。与人类不同，它无法设身处地为他人着想并分享他们的感受或经历。

sentences.en: If you listen carefully to Mylene's speech, you'll notice she says, " you know ", a lot.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细听Mylene的讲话，你会发现她经常说“你知道的”。

sentences.en: Phrases like, " you know ","um" and "ah" are called filler words and are used to give the speaker time to think, or to express uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 像“你知道的”、“嗯”和“啊”这样的短语被称为填充词，用于给说话者思考的时间，或者表达不确定。

sentences.en: Right, I think it's time I revealed the answer to my question, Phil.
sentences.zh: 好了，我想是时候揭晓我问题的答案了，Phil。

sentences.en: I asked you how many call centre workers are there globally.
sentences.zh: 我问你全球有多少呼叫中心员工。

sentences.en: And I said 17 million. Which is the right answer.
sentences.zh: 我说的是1700万。这是正确答案。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with yelling, another word for shouting.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们在本期节目中学到的词汇，首先是yelling（大喊大叫），这是shouting的另一个词。

sentences.en: To pacify someone means to calm them down when they're angry.
sentences.zh: To pacify someone（安抚某人）意味着当他们生气时让他们平静下来。

sentences.en: In the near future means very soon, or within a short time.
sentences.zh: In the near future（在不久的将来）意味着非常快，或者在很短的时间内。

sentences.en: The phrase, as a matter of fact is used to add emphasis to what you're saying, to give more detail about what you've just said, or to introduce something that contrasts with it.
sentences.zh: 短语 as a matter of fact（事实上）用于加强你所说的话的语气，提供关于你刚说过的话的更多细节，或者引入与之形成对比的内容。

sentences.en: If you're empathetic, you're able to put yourself in someone else's position and share their feelings or experiences.
sentences.zh: 如果你是 empathetic（有同理心的），你就能够设身处地为他人着想，分享他们的感受或经历。

sentences.en: And finally, filler words like 'um', 'ah' and ' you know' give the speaker more time to think, or to express uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 最后，像“嗯”、“啊”和“你知道的”这样的填充词给了说话者更多思考的时间，或者表达了不确定。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, Bye!
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，再见！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
